title: Indian Knoll: Late Archaic Shell Midden in Ohio County
summary: In Ohio County, Late Archaic hunter-gatherers returned for millennia to the Indian Knoll shell midden, which yielded over a thousand burials.
bodyMarkdown:
Five thousand years before the first stations, Late Archaic hunter-gatherers kept returning to a shell midden in Ohio County. Indian Knoll (15OH2) yielded over a thousand burials, twenty-three dog burials, and more than 50,000 artifacts—spear points, bone pins, marine shell beads, bannerstones—when University of Kentucky crews dug it in the late 1930s WPA years. People hunted deer, gathered hickory nuts, fished, and harvested river mussels.

In the early 1990s Indian Knoll and nineteen other Late Archaic shell middens became National Historic Landmarks, some of the deepest windows we have on Archaic life in the Ohio Valley.
Source: [https://archaeology.ky.gov/Find-a-Site/Pages/Indian-Knoll.aspx](https://archaeology.ky.gov/Find-a-Site/Pages/Indian-Knoll.aspx)
